tools.name: start_check
tools.description: Start a check of what AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile phones show when a number calls. Returns the test line to call ('dial') for each carrier and a check id (and a token for a keyless check: keep it). The number being checked must then call each test line within the window. tools.name: get_check
tools.description: The check and each carrier's result: status waiting, complete or incomplete; the label shown and caller name; flagged true/false; a screenshot link. Set wait_seconds (up to 25) to wait for results to arrive before answering.

tools.name: get_coverage
tools.description: Which carriers are online now, prices in cents, and the dialing window.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Needs a key. The account balance, holds, and this key's spending limit.

tools.name: request_approval
tools.description: Get a link (approve_url) for your human to open: they sign in, add funds if needed, set a spending limit and approve. Show them the link, then call get_approval. Use this when a check is refused with free_check_used, insufficient_funds or key_limit.

tools.name: get_approval
tools.description: Status of an approval request: pending, approved, declined or expired. Once approved, a keyless request returns api_key (shown once): pass it as api_key to the other tools. Set wait_seconds (up to 25) to wait for a decision.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_check" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.detail: Description of "get_approval" references sensitive artifacts (api_key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
